title: Why Double-Clicking 'Pay' Doesn't Charge You Twice (Idempotency)
audience: Junior backend devs, interview preppers, payments/SaaS builders
whyCare: Retries happen constantly; without an idempotency key, a timeout becomes a double charge. Payment APIs use this pattern.

evidence.claim: Gap: idempotency long-form leaders are small: 16,864 views (Coder's Gyan, 11 months), 15,274 (Java Techie, 4 months), 1,734 ('How Idempotency Keys Actually Work', 5 months)
Shorts demand exists: 'Implement API Idempotency In 3 Simple Steps' 28K views; 'Idempotency in Spring Boot | Interview Question' 21K views
Stripe API docs: idempotency keys let you safely retry requests "without accidentally performing the same operation twice"; retries with the same key return the saved response (checked 2026-10-20)

angle: Diagram: Phone -> Server -> Bank. First POST times out (cross), retry sends a second packet -> two charges (shake). Replay with key 'abc123': server checks its key table and returns the saved result (check). Code panel: one header line.
hook: Your payment timed out. You tap Pay again. Why aren't you charged twice?
strengths: Best gap of the set; universal 'double charge' fear; fits the Webhooks / Rate-limit series
weaknesses: Lower raw demand; 'idempotency' is jargon, so the title leads with the outcome
